title: Israel president asks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's rival, to form new government
summary: Israel's president has tapped opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, in another setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

image.caption: Gadi Eisenkot, Israeli opposition leader, speaks at an event in Tel Aviv on Oct. 25. (David Goldman/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Israel's president has tapped opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, in another setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Recent election left neither Eisenkot or Netanyahu with clear path to power
The move comes after a deadlocked election that that left neither man with a clear ​path to power.

Netanyahu, Israel's ⁠longest-serving leader, ⁠is ‌fighting to hold onto office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an ⁠Oct. 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc ‌in parliament.
An anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Eisenkot, an ex-military chief, has refused to ​join forces with Arab ⁠parties who could hand it a ⁠majority.
But Arab leaders, ⁠angered ⁠by policies ​of Netanyahu and his far-right allies, ​still ⁠nominated Eisenkot during marathon talks with President Isaac Herzog.

items: Arab parties offer Israel's political leaders a path to victory. Why does no one want to take it?
